chapter: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band
title: Mrs. Bessie L. Allen and the Sunday school behind the band
summary: Louis Thompson, the first member, recalls Mrs. Bessie L. Allen handing out instruments; her non-denominational Sunday school drew 500 children, and some parents distrusted her as a truant officer.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And then we had another guy named Louis Thompson, who was a bass player. He was one of the first. I think he was the first in this Sunday school band at the Booker T. Washington Community Center Band. Because I was talking to him. You know, when you're in there you don't figure out how it started or nothing. You're just there, you know. So we were talking since we've been here, not too long ago, and he says, "You know, I was the first one in that band." And I said, "Is that right?" Says, "Yes. She called me in and had a bin full of instruments, you know, and says pick out one, we're going to start a band." Yes, that was the first --
Mrs. Bessie L. Allen, A, double-l, e-n.
Oh, she was a wonderful woman, wasn't she?
A wonderful woman, and the way she got this money, she started this in Sunday school, and they had about 500 kids that would come there every Sunday.

Yeah, sure. It was a big Sunday school, and you all met in a big room, and then after you -- we played a little bit, the band played, and a little talking here and there, you know, and then you all went off to separate rooms. Some of the boys went to number one room, some of the boys in
number two room. Some of the girls in number one -- I think it was split up. And you'd go up there and they would give you a Bible, you know, and you'd read from the Bible.
No, this was no denomination. It was just --
Just all the children in the neighborhood.
She did this thing. And what a mind she had. I think about it. It's fantastic. The older I get the way I think about it, you know.
-- what could that woman have been -- you know, how she could think of such --

And a lot of people, you know, there's always somebody that don't like something. So a lot of people would say, 'Oh, no, I wouldn't have my kids go up there. She's a truant officer,' or something like that, you know, and she'll put you in a home, you know. And my mother paid no attention to it and I guess a lot of other mothers didn't either.
